Posted April 4, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
Currently, the entire Drug War establishment seems to be in a major panic over the prospect of Maryland lowering the penalty for possession of one ounce of cannabis to a $100 fine for people who can prove a medical necessity.

Frankly, the bill is such a farce that it will do little to help most patients, but one would think that it was making cannabis mandatory for toddlers. Why such a reaction to such an inconsequential bill?
See
 DEA Says THC Is Safe. "! As The Volume Of Prohibitionist Propaganda Goes Up, The Quality Goes Down. Drug Czar Makes A Fool of Himself In Maryland. DEA Now Sending Emails Against Medical Cannabis.

Meanwhile, the Drug Czar's office has announced that it is dropping its goofy ads that try to link users of illicit substances with terrorism, but they will be redirecting the money to pay for more ads, supposedly aimed at children, that lie about the government's own data on cannabis.

Consequently, this Administration's version of the Drug War is perhaps more fixated with cannabis than any other, and that is saying a lot.
See
Marijuana Bigger Problem Than Meth? DEAland And The Bush Administration Have a Very Serious Walters Problem. We Couldn't Make This Up!
and
The Seemingly Inexhaustible Torrent Of Prohibitionist Propaganda Reminds Me Of The Greek Myth About Hercules And The Stables Of King Augeas. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Late last month, the Drug Enforcement Administration published its final rules on hemp foods, essentially banning the sale of all hemp food products by April 21, 2003. (Their choice of dates is amusing, but I think that the 9th Circuit is very likely to block it once again.)

This is taking cannabiphobia to new depths of absurdity.
See
http://www.VoteHemp.com
And to show that it is not a purely DEAland problem, see
The Irrationality of Hemp Seed Oil Policies in Canada -- Yes, Canada And Australia Show that Marijuana Prohibition Is A Threat to Everyone.

What is going on here? Is this the result of a rational policy or of a cult?

Let me emphasize that when I compare the current anti-cannabis policies to a cult, I am not making a rhetorical point about the Bush/Ashcroft axis of ostentatious religiosity. Rather, there are real parallels to the workings of cults.

In the 1930s, Germany was probably the technologically most advanced country in the world, so when the Nazis came to power, one aspect of their ideology was called scientific racism. A Canadian historian, Modris Ecksteins, described the Nazi ideology as being a cult based on irrationalism crossed with technicism. Sound familiar?

Today, officials of the most scientifically advanced country tell us that science says that there is no such thing as medical cannabis. The prohibitionists invoke the word science at every turn. Who can be against science?
See
 Arizona Columnist Demonstrates Devastating Effect of Prohibitionism On The Mind; Gateway To The Irrational? 2 Columns

The disadvantage of such a system is that it makes rational retreat impossible without losing the cadre. The cannabiphobic cult is the hard core constituency of the drug war in general. Hence the suppression of hemp is more important than heroin.

It is at times like this when the excesses of the cannabiphobic cult are at their most extreme that the system generates the most opposition. To paraphrase Dickens, this really is the best of times and the worst of times.

We must have the courage and conviction that sustained Martin Luther King, Jr. We have to believe that we will win because we are appealing to the fundamental values of a society built on personal freedom.

If one does not believe that truth and love must ultimately triumph over lies and hatred, then Well, join a cult.
